title: The Grave Digger
text: An old man digs graves among the barrows, steady and unhurried, his spade ringing on stone. There are far more open graves than there are dead. He says, without looking up, that they will be needed. He has dug them to size.

options.label: Ask him who the graves are for. You would rather know.

outcomes.text: He names a rival House, and keeps digging, and does not look up. You do not ask about the others.

options.label: The strongest helps him dig, so that the graves are ready when needed.

outcomes.text: He gives them his spare shovel, blessed against the dead. They will need it, he says.

options.label: Fill in his graves. Nobody needs to be buried today.

outcomes.text: He weeps, and the barrows stir, waiting for their beds, and growing impatient.
